bibliographic.authors: Sivan Schwartz, Avi Yaeli, Segev Shlomov
bibliographic.venue: AutoMate'23@IJCAI: The First International Workshop on the Future of No-Code Digital Apprentices; CEUR Workshop Proceedings
bibliographic.citation_apa: Schwartz, S., Yaeli, A., & Shlomov, S. (2023). Enhancing trust in LLM-based AI automation agents: New considerations and future challenges. methodology.method_family: literature synthesis and nascent product evaluation
methodology.study_design: conceptual framework paper analyzing trust dimensions for LLM-based automation agents, with assessment of selected commercial/nascent products
methodology.sample_description: Existing trust literature and frameworks; several nascent LLM-based automation products (e.g., Microsoft CoPilot, Adept.AI, MultiOn, chatGPT, Watson Orchestrate)
methodology.sector: process automation; no-code digital apprentices; enterprise AI assistants
methodology.technology_context: LLM-based autonomous AI automation agents (AutoGPT, AgentGPT, LangChain, ChatGPT Plugins, GPT-3, ChatGPT, GPT-4) integrated into no-code automation and digital assistant products

eligibility.decision_rationale: The paper directly addresses trust considerations for LLM-based AI automation agents, synthesizing trust components from prior literature and evaluating how nascent products address them. It aligns with governance, accountability, transparency, privacy, security, and human-in-the-loop themes relevant to the review, but focuses on process automation trust rather than conversational governance in explicitly regulated high-stakes domains.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only partial full text was provided (fragments from pages 1-3 and 8); complete sections on trust categories, product evaluation, and future challenges are referenced but not fully available for appraisal.

appraisal.notes: Clear conceptual objective to analyze trust in LLM-based automation agents and evaluate nascent products, but provided text lacks detail on product selection criteria, evaluation protocol, and explicit study limitations. Non-empirical design limits sampling and data-collection appraisal.

cerqual.explanation: Findings on trust considerations for LLM automation agents are logically structured and relevant to governance-of-trust themes, but confidence is moderated by incomplete full text, unclear product sampling, and absence of empirical validation in regulated conversational settings.

coding.theme: Trust frameworks for LLM-based AI automation agents
coding.subtheme: Mapping legacy trust dimensions to autonomous LLM agents and assessing nascent products

synthesis.main_claim: Rapid advances in LLMs and LLM-based agent frameworks create new trust challenges and opportunities for AI-based process automation agents that differ from prior trust frameworks.
synthesis.contribution: Synthesizes existing trust-in-AI literature, identifies considerations specific to LLM-based automation agents, evaluates how nascent products address these topics, and outlines future research challenges.
synthesis.limitations: Conceptual and product-review design without reported empirical study in regulated domains; incomplete provided text limits verification of evaluation depth, product selection, and stated limitations.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence for trust, transparency, responsibility, privacy, security, and human-in-the-loop considerations in LLM-based agent governance; complement with studies focused on regulated conversational systems and operational governance mechanisms.

evidence.excerpt: Trust can be divided into two categories, (1) cognitive trust, and (2) emotional trust.
